name: Sea Aster
description: Late summer blooming covering saltmarshes in pale purple.

name: Glasswort
description: Fleshy stems turn brilliant red and orange in autumn.

name: Sea Purslane
description: Silvery-grey leaves with tiny yellow flowers forming dense coastal mats.

name: Marram Grass
description: Tall seed heads sway on the dunes of West Wittering.

name: Sea Bindweed
description: Large pink and white trumpet flowers bloom across the sand dunes.

name: Sea Holly
description: Striking metallic blue, thistle-like blooms on sandy shores.

name: Sea Campion
description: Carpets of delicate white flowers with swollen, bladder-like calyxes.

name: Thrift
description: Dense cushions of bright pink flowers bloom on the saltmarsh edges.

name: Yellow Horned-poppy
description: Vibrant yellow blooms followed by distinctive long, curved seed pods.

name: Sea Rocket
description: Fleshy leaves and pale lilac flowers appear along the strandline.

name: Sea Spurge
description: Architectural blue-green foliage with small yellow-green flowers.

name: Viper's Bugloss
description: Tall spikes of intense blue flowers attract multitudes of coastal bees.

name: Pyramidal Orchid
description: Vivid pink, cone-shaped flower spikes emerge in the dune slacks.

name: Southern Marsh Orchid
description: Robust stems with purple patterned flowers bloom in damp coastal meadows.

name: English Scurvygrass
description: Early flowering white clusters appear on muddy banks and creeks.

name: Common Sea-lavender
description: Widespread misty purple blooms turn the summer saltmarsh vibrant.

name: Golden Samphire
description: Bright yellow daisy-like flowers adorn the higher shingle and marsh.

name: Sea Wormwood
description: Aromatic silver foliage peaks in late summer before autumn winds.

name: Cordgrass
description: Flowering spikes emerge, helping bind the mudflats together.

name: Sea Beet
description: Glossy green leaves and subtle green flowering spikes appear on the shingle.

name: Bittersweet
description: Bright red poisonous berries dangle from scrambling vines.

name: Rock Samphire
description: Umbels of yellowish-green flowers bloom on shingle and coastal defenses.

name: Sea Mayweed
description: Daisy-like blooms with thick fleshy leaves grow at the high tide mark.

name: Hound's-tongue
description: Dull reddish-purple flowers bloom on dune grasslands.

name: Evening Primrose
description: Large yellow flowers open at dusk to attract night-flying moths.

name: Roe Deer
description: Bucks aggressively chase does during the mid-summer rut.

name: Red Fox
description: Fox cubs emerge from their earths to play in the spring twilight.

name: Brown Hare
description: Mad March hares box in the fields surrounding the harbour.

name: European Badger
description: Young cubs begin foraging outside the sett during warm spring evenings.

name: Common Pipistrelle
description: Bats swarm and feed heavily on insects before hibernation.

name: Water Vole
description: Active feeding and territory marking along the freshwater ditches.

name: Common Lizard
description: Basking in the open on the warm sand dunes of East Head.

name: Slow Worm
description: Mating season sees these legless lizards tangling together in the undergrowth.

name: Grass Snake
description: Swimming hunting expeditions through the coastal grazing marsh ditches.

name: Adder
description: Males perform the 'dance of the adders' to establish dominance.

name: Stag Beetle
description: Males fly clumsily at dusk on warm summer evenings looking for mates.

name: Marbled White Butterfly
description: Striking black and white butterflies emerge over the coastal grasslands.

name: Sand Wasp
description: Females dig burrows in the dunes and drag paralyzed caterpillars inside.

name: Painted Lady Butterfly
description: Mass migrations arrive from North Africa across the Channel.

name: Hummingbird Hawk-moth
description: Hovering like tiny birds to feed on viper's bugloss and sea bindweed.

name: Wasp Spider
description: Large striped females spin orb webs in the tall dune grasses.

name: Emperor Dragonfly
description: Large, aggressive males endlessly patrol coastal ponds.

name: Broad-bodied Chaser
description: Freshly emerged dragonflies hunt over the marshland ditches.

name: Common Darter
description: Late-season dragonflies sunning themselves on wooden boardwalks.

name: Roesel's Bush-cricket
description: Continuous high-pitched buzzing fills the air in tall grass.

name: Glow-worm
description: Females emit a steady green glow at night to attract flying males.

name: Buff-tailed Bumblebee
description: Large queens emerge from hibernation to forage on early coastal blossoms.

name: Six-spot Burnet Moth
description: Day-flying red and black moths swarm the dune flowers.

name: Cinnabar Moth
description: Striking yellow and black caterpillars devour ragwort on the dunes.

name: Common Toad
description: Mass migrations to breeding ponds result in loud spawning congregations.

name: Brent Goose
description: Thousands arrive from Siberia, forming massive, noisy winter flocks.

name: Dunlin
description: Huge winter flocks perform synchronized aerial murmurations over the mudflats.

name: Black-tailed Godwit
description: Probing the winter mudflats with their long, straight bills.

name: Oystercatcher
description: Loud, high-pitched piping displays echo across the harbour.

name: Curlew
description: Evocative bubbling calls ring out across the winter estuarine mud.

name: Redshank
description: Noisy 'wardens of the marsh' perform yodeling display flights.

name: Ringed Plover
description: Camouflaged breeding and protective distraction displays on the shingle.

name: Little Tern
description: Chattering summer visitors plunge-diving for fish in the shallow creeks.

name: Common Tern
description: Elaborate aerial courtship and fish-offering displays.

name: Sandwich Tern
description: Noisy, grating calls as they dive steeply into the harbour waters.

name: Shelduck
description: Adults escort large crèches of ducklings across the mud at low tide.

name: Wigeon
description: Flocks of grazing ducks fill the air with sharp, whistling calls.

name: Teal
description: Males perform intricate head-flicking courtship displays on the water.

name: Pintail
description: Elegant ducks gather in courtship groups, rearing up in the water.

name: Lapwing
description: Tumbling, acrobatic flight displays over the coastal grazing marshes.

name: Skylark
description: Continuous, complex songs delivered from high hovering flights over the dunes.

name: Meadow Pipit
description: Parachuting display flights from the scrub to the saltmarsh.

name: Reed Bunting
description: Males sing their simple, repetitive song from prominent reed stems.

name: Cetti's Warbler
description: Sudden, explosive bursts of song from deep within the damp scrub.

name: Sedge Warbler
description: Scratchy, erratic flight songs over the reedbeds and ditches.

name: Reed Warbler
description: Rhythmic, churring song echoing continuously through the phragmites reeds.

name: Little Egret
description: Displaying striking white nuptial plumes during the breeding season.

name: Grey Heron
description: Noisy clattering and bill-snapping in the heronries during nesting.

name: Osprey
description: Stopping over to fish in the harbour during their autumn migration south.

name: Marsh Harrier
description: Breathtaking sky-dancing displays high above the reedbeds.

name: Harbour Seal
description: Mothers give birth to pups on the secluded mudbanks.

name: Grey Seal
description: Hauling out on the sandbanks at low tide in larger numbers.

name: Bottlenose Dolphin
description: Occasional summer pods chase fish into the harbour mouth.

name: European Bass
description: Spawning adults migrate into the warmer, shallower harbour waters.

name: Grey Mullet
description: Large shoals cruise just below the surface in the shallow creeks.

name: European Eel
description: Tiny transparent elvers migrate from the sea into freshwater streams.

name: Atlantic Mackerel
description: Fast-moving shoals hunt small fry near the harbour entrance.

name: Cuttlefish
description: Arrive in the shallow harbour waters to mate and lay black 'sea grape' eggs.

name: Native Oyster
description: Mass spawning events release millions of larvae into the tidal currents.

name: Shore Crab
description: Moulting crabs seek shelter while soft, and mating pairs embrace.

name: Edible Crab
description: Adults migrate inshore to breed and feed in the harbour's rocky margins.

name: European Lobster
description: Berried (egg-carrying) females move into shallower waters.

name: Common Prawn
description: Rockpools and eelgrass beds teem with translucent, darting prawns.

name: Snakelocks Anemone
description: Bright green, purple-tipped tentacles fully expand in the warming waters.

name: Beadlet Anemone
description: Releasing fully-formed miniature young into the water column.

name: Common Starfish
description: Mass congregations feed aggressively on the rich mussel beds.

name: Moon Jellyfish
description: Pulsing swarms bloom in the warm, nutrient-rich summer waters.

name: Compass Jellyfish
description: Distinctive V-shaped marked jellies drift in with the summer tides.

name: Lugworm
description: Millions of sand casts appear on the mudflats at low tide.

name: Ragworm
description: Mass spawning swarms perform frantic nuptial dances at the surface.

name: Dwarf Eelgrass
description: Tiny underwater flowers bloom and release seeds onto the mudflats.

name: Common Eelgrass
description: Dense underwater meadows reach their peak growth, providing crucial nursery habitats.

name: Sea Lettuce
description: Explosive bright green algal blooms cover the nutrient-rich mud.

name: Bladder Wrack
description: Swollen fruiting bodies release gametes into the spring tides.

name: Peacock Worm
description: Elegant fan-like crowns extend from muddy tubes to filter feed.
